records.description: Sickingenbrücke is a bridge area in Berlin-Moabit, where Sickingenstraße crosses the water near Neues Ufer and the industrial approaches towards Mierendorffplatz. Both gay-szene and Planet Randy carry older mentions of cruising around the bridge and underpass, sometimes describing late evenings. There are no readable dated visits from the previous year establishing that the scene continues, and the main detailed directory page could not be reopened during this review. Nearby canal paths and industrial watersides may have private or restricted sections, so a historic mention should not be treated as an invitation to enter fenced land. This is a potentially identifiable location, but its exact meeting point, current crowd and practical timing are unknown. It stays on hold rather than being listed as active.
records.tags: Bridge, Canal, Industrial Area, Historical Reports
records.opening_notes: No verified recent hours or safe subarea.

records.description: Theodor-Heuss-Platz in Berlin-Westend has an old-fashioned public men's toilet that is still discussed as a cruising meeting point. The facility is on the square itself, close to U Theodor-Heuss-Platz, with reports referring to the urinals and cubicles rather than the nearby park. May and July 2026 first-person posts describe encounters, including one late after 01:00, but several other July visitors found nobody, so there's no guaranteed busy period. The crowd seems variable rather than reliably tied to any specific age range. A particularly important warning comes from a 17 May 2026 visitor who reported aggressive homophobic abuse and a kick to the door during a visit. It's a public toilet, not a private play space; opening conditions and other users must be respected, and anyone going should take the harassment risk seriously.
records.tags: Public Restroom, Urban, Mixed Reports, Recent Activity, Safety Warning
records.opening_notes: Recent visitor report mentions activity after 01:00, but other visits were empty. Actual WC hours uncertain.

records.description: Volkspark Mariendorf in southern Berlin offers rolling lawns, wooded paths and a pond often called Ententeich. Older gay directories present the park as a possible cruising location, and an April 2026 contributor wrote about noticing men around the pond and later meeting someone. However, those experiences were described retrospectively without exact event dates, and another regular visitor in the same month found little or no cruising on the hill. The material doesn't establish a particular path, repeatable busy period or typical age group. There are also families and ordinary park users throughout the grounds. The park is straightforward to access as public green space, but for Backroom the current evidence is not yet precise enough to recommend a defined cruising location rather than a large general park.
blockers: Possible encounters dated only by retrospective post

records.description: At the edge of Volkspark Wilmersdorf, older gay guides identify a public toilet under the name Klappe am Volkspark. Planet Randy places it on Am Volkspark and recommends mornings or after work, while CruisingGays describes a toilet near Uhlandstraße 110 and U Blissestraße, potentially a different facility. One guide implies access throughout the night; the other says the toilets are locked at night. Neither carries a verified 2026 visit resolving those contradictions. The park itself is a popular neighbourhood recreation area, but that doesn't establish a working cruising toilet. It's important to identify the correct building and its actual operating hours before sending someone there. Until then, even the claimed best time and crowd are historical guesses.
records.address: Am Volkspark, Wilmersdorf, Berlin (specific toilet uncertain)
records.tags: Public Restroom, Park Edge, Historical Reports, Potential Duplicate
records.opening_notes: Old guide suggests morning/after work; another states toilets locked late at night.

records.description: The A57 motorway service-area listings for Esch and Weiler refer to two separate parking stops near Köln-Chorweiler and Pulheim: Esch on the eastern side and Weiler on the western side. Old cruising directories mention activity around both, with no fixed timetable. A May 2026 visitor said much of the vegetation had been cleared since the preceding autumn, leaving the formerly secluded parking areas more exposed to passing traffic. The clearest recent positive encounter report is from September 2025, before the current twelve-month cutoff, so it cannot establish today's scene. These areas can only be approached safely from their designated motorway direction. Never cross the carriageways or enter closed roadside land, and don't expect the old bushes or a reliable crowd to still be there.
blockers: 2026 report concerns loss of privacy, not recent encounter
Two distinct car parks need separate identification
records.address: A57 motorway, Weiler westbound / Esch eastbound, Cologne-Chorweiler
